summary.text: Named among the fifty-seven suitors from Dulichium and again among the Same wooers in Apollodorus' island catalogues — distinct from the suitor of the same name from Zacynthus (Epitome 7.29) and from the son of Laomedon so called at Troy.

story.text: Apollodorus names Clytius among the suitors who devoured Odysseus' substance, listed after Evenorides and before Agenor in the long company of Penelope's wooers.

The same name appears again among the wooers Apollodorus assigns to Same in Epitome 7.28 — listed after Eteoneus and before Prothous — one figure, or a namesake from another island, the Epitome does not say.
Apollodorus rolls Clytius on both the Dulichium island list (Epitome 7.27) and the Same catalogue (7.28) — one suitor or two of the same name, the Epitome does not say.
